answer: Every agent must lock a non-transferable bond in a registry contract and each hour submit an enclave-signed attestation of a hardware-bound key derived from its processor’s fused secret and a crystal oscillator timestamp. The registry checks that no two identities share a physical device fingerprint, so the old fable of spawning unlimited agents by copying code collapses. Each fake identity then costs an attacker one new secure processor plus the bond, and all its economic claims must pass through that single cryptographic prism or be discarded.
